record_type_quote:
In this article, we undertook a narrow replication of Van Ryzin's (2013) study and
conducted an empirical generalization by extending the original study to Hong Kong and Shenzhen to see if the find-
ings hold and are valid in this context.

targets.title: An experimental test of the expectancy-disconfirmation theory of citizen satisfaction.
targets.evidence_quote:
In this article, we undertook a narrow replication of Van Ryzin's (2013) study and
conducted an empirical generalization by extending the original study to Hong Kong and Shenzhen to see if the find-
ings hold and are valid in this context.
targets.outcome_quote:
We can therefore conclude that we replicated the study by Van Ryzin (2013)
and that the consistency of the findings suggests that the expectancy-disconfirmation model holds promise in a vari-
ety of settings as a framework for measuring citizen satisfaction with public services.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly conclude that they replicated the study as a whole. That overall verdict governs under rule 1, despite the subsequent discussion of differences in individual relationships, including the Hong Kong interaction and net expectations effect. The two replications are identified by cities, without numbered study labels.

reasoning: Completed new-sample experimental replications in Hong Kong and Shenzhen explicitly re-test Van Ryzin (2013). Other Van Ryzin works and subsequent replications supply background, rather than additional targets.
